patterns.name: Colon-Split Headings
patterns.oneLiner: 'Smart Scheduling: Plan Your Week In Seconds.' Every heading is a label, a colon, then a slogan.
patterns.fix: Write a heading that says one thing. Either name the feature or state the benefit; put the other in the body. Ban colons in headings in the copy brief and rewrite any that survive.

patterns.name: Bold-Label Bullets
patterns.oneLiner: Every list item starts with a bolded label and a colon, then a sentence that repeats the label.
patterns.fix: Write lists as plain items that each carry one fact, or as short paragraphs. If a label is genuinely needed, make it a real heading or a definition list, and delete any sentence that only restates its label.

patterns.name: Whether You're A
patterns.oneLiner: 'Whether you're a solo founder or a global enterprise, X has you covered.'
patterns.fix: Name the one audience the product is actually built for and the situation they are in. If it truly serves two groups, give each its own section with a concrete reason.

patterns.name: The Conclusion Heading
patterns.oneLiner: Every blog post and guide ends with an H2 called 'Conclusion' that starts 'In conclusion'.
patterns.fix: End an article where the last useful point ends. If a summary is needed, put it at the top as a short answer. Rewrite openings to start with the specific problem, not the state of the world.

patterns.name: Markdown Showing Through
patterns.oneLiner: Literal **asterisks**, ## hashes and [brackets](links) printed on the page as text.
patterns.fix: Either render Markdown deliberately with a sanitising parser, or ask the model for plain text and strip Markdown before saving. Add a pre-publish check that fails on '**', a leading '#' or '](' in visible text.

patterns.name: Compliance Badge Cosplay
patterns.oneLiner: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR and ISO badges in the footer of a product with no report behind any of them.
patterns.fix: Show a compliance mark only when you hold a current, clean report and are entitled to the logo; link to a trust page that names the auditor and report date. Otherwise describe your actual security practices in plain words.

patterns.name: The Unbacked Superlative
patterns.oneLiner: 'The world's first', 'the #1 AI platform', '10x faster', with nothing behind the number.
patterns.fix: Remove any rank, 'first' or multiplier you cannot cite. Replace it with a specific, checkable outcome from a named customer or your own measured benchmark, and link the method.

patterns.name: The Generated Privacy Policy
patterns.oneLiner: A privacy policy that exists, sounds legal, and describes a generic company's data practices.
patterns.fix: Inventory what the app collects, where it goes and which vendors process it, then write or generate the policy from that list with the real legal entity, contact and jurisdiction. Re-check it whenever a tracking script or AI vendor is added.

patterns.name: The Raw Error Leak
patterns.oneLiner: 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_key"' shown to the customer in a toast.
patterns.fix: Map known error codes to plain messages that say what happened and what to do ('That email already has an account. Sign in instead.'). Log the raw error server-side; never render error.message from a database or SDK to users.

patterns.name: The Untitled Dialog
patterns.oneLiner: Mobile menus and modals open as dialogs with no title, so screen readers announce just 'dialog'.
patterns.fix: Give every dialog and sheet a DialogTitle or SheetTitle (visually hidden if the design has none) and a description where useful. Treat Radix accessibility warnings as build failures.

patterns.name: Wrong Page Language
patterns.oneLiner: A Spanish, German or Sinhala site whose HTML still declares lang="en".
patterns.fix: Set lang to the page's actual language in the root layout (and per page for multilingual sites); mark inline foreign phrases with their own lang. Add a check that compares the declared language with the detected language of the body text.

patterns.name: The Token Firehose
patterns.oneLiner: A streaming AI answer is announced to screen readers over and over as it grows, or not at all.
patterns.fix: Announce state, not tokens: a polite live message 'Generating' then 'Response ready' (or the full reply once complete), with focus or a shortcut to jump to it. Never put the streaming node itself in an atomic live region.

patterns.name: Enter Sends Mid-Word
patterns.oneLiner: Typing Japanese, Chinese or Korean in the AI chat box sends a half-composed message on Enter.
patterns.fix: Ignore Enter while event.isComposing is true (and on keyCode 229 for Safari), and test the composer with at least one IME. Offer Shift+Enter or a setting for Enter behaviour.

patterns.name: Scroll Hijacked By The Stream
patterns.oneLiner: You scroll up to read the start of the answer, and the view keeps following the newest line.
patterns.fix: Follow the stream only while the user is already at the bottom; stop on any wheel, touch or key scroll and show a 'Jump to latest' button. Consider anchoring the start of the response at the top of the viewport instead.

patterns.name: The Eaten Prompt
patterns.oneLiner: A long prompt fails to send, and the text box comes back empty.
patterns.fix: Clear the composer only after the server accepts the message; on any failure restore the text and attachments. Persist drafts locally per conversation so reloads, sign-ins and limits do not lose them.
